title: Entropy-normalized microbatcher with early-stall detection for streaming chat
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: Streaming chat workloads with long-lived sessions cause fragmented microbatches and uneven GPU memory pressure because KV cache sizes vary drastically by session. The current time/window-based microbatcher sometimes waits on low-entropy turns (clients sending short prompts or expecting short replies) which produces long waits and spikes in per-GPU KV memory. This leads to higher latency p95 and occasional OOMs on high-density hosts. Goal: implement a new batch formation heuristic — the "entropy-normalized microbatcher" — combined with an early-stall detection system and lightweight KV-tiling eviction hints to (1) reduce p95 streaming tail latency, (2) smooth GPU memory utilization across slabs, and (3) avoid end-user stalls/504s when hosts approach memory pressure. Scope: runtime changes to batcher and session metadata, small agent to annotate KV cache hotness, and a conservative rollout path behind a config flag. Non-goals: rewriting kernel-level GPU allocation — we rely on slab reservations and existing allocator APIs. Success metrics: reduce streaming p95 latency by >=10% on convo-heavy models, reduce host OOM rate by 95% in synthetic KV-heavy tests, and preserve model quality (no measurable degradation in next-token perplexity on held-out eval sets).
approach:
Heuristic summary:
1) Entropy-normalized priority score: for each incoming request we compute a microheuristic score = normalized(next-token entropy) / sqrt(session_kv_weight) * urgency_boost, where session_kv_weight = clipped(KV_size_bytes / session_budget_bytes, 0.1, 4.0). The estimator uses the runtime's cached softmax logits when available or an inexpensive n-gram fallback for extremely short prompts. Lower entropy (more predictable next token) yields higher bundling affinity because these requests typically finish faster and benefit from coalescing.
2) Early-stall detection: track per-batch queue_wait_ms and per-host gpu_mem_pct. If queue_wait_ms > 35ms and predicted batch completion time exceeds stall_threshold, force immediate flush of pending microbatch and activate fast-path single-request scheduling for the next N requests from that session.
3) KV-tiling eviction hints: add a lightweight per-session "tiling_score" combining recency, token-entropy, and generation-length heuristic. If a session's tiling_score falls below a threshold, mark it as a candidate for KV compaction (eviction to disk or lower-priority slab). This is advisory for the allocator; the allocator decides final eviction.
4) Slab reservation combinator: maintain a small adaptive reservation per host for high-entropy sessions so that unpredictable sessions do not force full compaction during peaks. Reservation size is a percentile-based function (e.g., reserve min(12GB, 90th-percentile session_kv)).
design_decisions:
Trade-offs considered:
- We could use strict recency-based eviction (LRU) but that ignores predictability. Entropy gives a signal about remaining generation length, which empirically correlates with how quickly a KV will be unused.
- Aggressive eviction reduces memory but increases recompute/cache-miss cost; we choose advisory eviction with allocator-level final decision to avoid quality regressions.
- Early flush reduces average wait but can increase microbatch count (more small batches). To limit throughput regression we apply early-stall heuristics only when predicted GPU-mem_pct > 78% or when queue_wait_ms consistently exceeds 35ms for 3 consecutive windows.
- Complexity vs observability: All new signals are instrumented (entropy, tiling_score, stall_events) to allow rapid rollback if we see regressions.
implementation_plan:
1) Runtime: Add entropy estimator hook and session_kv_weight field to session metadata (ENG runtime change).
2) Batcher: Compute priority score at enqueue-time; sort within short-window buckets (5-10ms) rather than global sort to bound scheduling latency.
3) Eviction hints: emit tiling_score to allocator via existing metadata API; allocator accepts 'hint' and logs decisions.
4) Early-stall detector: host agent aggregates queue_wait_ms and gpu_mem_pct; triggers policy switch.
5) Feature flag + rollout: start with 5% hosts (canary), then 25%, 50%, 100% after validation.
6) Observability: dashboards for p50/p95/p99 latency, host OOMs, KV eviction count, and model quality regressions.
7) Docs + runbook: update Console rollout docs and incident playbook if nodes see OOMs.

experiments_and_results:
Local microbench harness (synth-convo-heavy):
- Baseline: p95 streaming latency 820ms, host OOMs 4/1k runs, avg gpu_mem_pct 74.3%
- Entropy microbatcher (canary config): p95 730ms (-11%), host OOMs 0/1k runs, avg gpu_mem_pct 69.8%
- With early-stall aggressive flush: p95 710ms (-13.4%), throughput reduced by 3.2% under max-load synthetic test.
Notes: Per-session perplexity on next-token eval held stable within 0.2% absolute delta. KV eviction readbacks increased 18% but recompute CPU time remained within acceptable limits on Dedicated hosts. Full fleet synthetic (subset of 200 hosts) runs pending; initial canary passed latency and OOM thresholds.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Canary (5% hosts) shows: p95 streaming latency reduction >=8% and no increase in user-facing errors.
2) No production OOMs traceable to the change during 72-hour canary.
3) KV eviction + recompute cost increase < 25% CPU on average for affected hosts.
4) Observability metrics (entropy, tiling_score, stall_events) instrumented and alerting thresholds defined.
5) Approved design review with PM and SRE and completed security checklist.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Eviction hints cause quality regressions if allocator over-evicts. Mitigation: keep hints advisory and add conservative knob to reduce eviction aggressiveness.
- Risk: Entropy estimator overhead increases per-request CPU. Mitigation: fast-path approximate estimator with early bailout for short prompts; memoize per-session where possible.
- Risk: Increased small microbatches reduce GPU throughput. Mitigation: limit early-stall flush to high-pressure conditions and bounded rate of single-request fast-path activation.
- Risk: Telemetry noise. Mitigation: add tagging to correlate events with feature-flag cohorts and host types.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + local harness (complete).
- Phase 1 (canary 5%): enable on low-risk regions and GPU types; monitor 48 hours.
- Phase 2 (expanded 25%): after passing canary metrics for 72 hours.
- Phase 3 (50%): 1 week observation.
- Phase 4 (full): gradual ramp to 100% with rollback window.
Rollback criteria: spike in host OOMs, p95 latency regression >3% vs baseline, or customer-facing error rate increase.
Runbook: If OOMs observed revert config and trigger allocator throttle; contact SRE on-call.
